title: Laksa Lemak
subtitle: Malaysian coconut curry noodle soup
excerpt: The richer, creamier Malaysian laksa: rice noodles in a deeply spiced coconut broth with prawns, tofu, and bean sprouts, built on a laksa paste of lemongrass, galangal, chilli, and candlenut. A bowl with many layers of flavour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Laksa lemak (lemak means rich or fat, referring to the coconut milk) is a variant of laksa associated with the Straits Chinese (Peranakan) community of Penang and Kuala Lumpur, distinct from the sour asam laksa that uses tamarind instead of coconut. The dish showcases the Peranakan fusion of Chinese and Malay culinary traditions: Chinese noodles and tofu in a Malay-spiced coconut broth. The paste is the foundation; making it from scratch rather than using commercial paste produces a significantly better result. Candlenuts (or macadamia as a substitute) are ground into the paste to add body and a subtle richness. The broth should be fragrant, creamy, and mildly hot, with the aromatics clearly present.

content.text: Fry the paste in oil before adding the coconut milk; this step is called tumis and takes 5 to 8 minutes over medium heat until the paste has darkened and the oil begins to separate from it. Skipping this step produces a raw, flat-tasting broth. Do not boil the broth vigorously once the coconut milk is in; it will curdle.

items.preparation: thick round rice noodles; soaked in cold water for 20 minutes and drained
fried until golden; cut into slices
white part only; sliced; for the paste
toasted; for the paste; or 4 macadamia nuts

content.text: Blend the lemongrass, galangal, chillies, shallots, garlic, turmeric, and toasted coconut with a splash of water to a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and fry, stirring constantly, for 6 to 8 minutes until darkened, very fragrant, and the oil is beginning to separate from the paste.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Add the coconut milk and fish sauce. Do not boil. Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until pink. Season with salt.
Divide the noodles between bowls. Pour the hot broth over with prawns. Add sliced fried tofu, bean sprouts, and spring onion. Serve with lime wedges.
